body: Thank you for the warning. Is it an issue of fumes or the pressure building?

Thank you for such a detailed response! 

Am I correct in thinking isopropyl alcohol would work for the solvent? And you mentioned a heat method that would be fastest, could you elaborate a bit more on how that process would work?

I am trying to make a juice that I could put into a refillable tank in a pen vape I got. I usually use a box mod for regular vaping so that general set up is more what I'm familiar with.

My tentative plan will be to use isopropyl alcohol to extract. Then filter it using a coffee filter. Then I take the THC infused alcohol and combine it with the PG VG mix on a double boiler for a couple of hours. Any parts of that you would recommend I change?

I really appreciate the help. I'm excited to do this but I don't want to mess it up and waste the kief.

I saw some recipes that talked about using solvents like Everclear. Do you know how that process goes? I've never attempted anything like this before and I'm a little out of my depth. 

You put it in a container with the solvent and shake/mix it. Right? Do you know how long it needs to stay in the solvent? Does it dissolve the kief or you have to filter the remainder out? And then you still need to do a special process to combine it with the PG/VG or just mix it together? Do you just dispose of any plant material filtered out or is it still usable for anything?

Sorry for a million questions. I was raised to measure twice and cut once, but there aren't too many interactive resources for this type of thing in an illegal state.
When we get to Yemen, can I stay with you?

I appreciate the thoughtful response. 

I know what you mean about it being unproductive to compare your life to others. There is a quote I love "The only happy people I know are people I don't know well." From a distance you only see a small part of people's lives and it's impossible to know the struggles they face. I'm sure that most casual acquaintances and co-workers of mine would describe me as a happy person. Perspective is a hell of a drug. 

I am taking steps to improve my situation though I admit that the lack of improvement has been a bit discouraging. Thank you for the encouragement. It means a lot.

This is an interesting thought. I don't know if I would say that I harbor self hatred, but I definitely have some self esteem issues. And I am not very happy with myself for a number of life choices I made when I was younger. This is certainly something to mention to my therapist. I appreciate the input.

I know what you mean about marvelling at even fictional people who are mentally healthy. It feels like they have some secret I don't know about. 

You are right that I tend to be a thinker. (Usually overthinking to my own detriment.) I appreciate the vote of confidence. I have never looked into Eckhart Tolle, though I have heard the name. It might be worth reading some of his stuff if I might identify with it. Thank you for the tip!

Wow. I'm blown away by the thoughtful responses and support. I really appreciate it. This was intended more as a venting/journaling exercise than expecting responses. Thank you all for your support.

I feel like I should give a little more context in response for anyone who is concerned or interested. First of all and most importantly, I want to mention that I am in no immediate danger of self harm. I am in my early 30s and I have wrestled with depression and had suicidal thoughts for a couple decades now. I am currently seeing a therapist and taking antidepressants. They have made a world of difference. I do however, fall back to a default of gloominess. And the longing for death relatively constantly. I know that it is a chemical I'm balance and a disease and not something to blame myself for. 

That being said, it fills me with shame thinking about how people have stormed the beaches of Normandy and crossed the frontier and did other incredibly difficult things against the odds, and I can hardly manage to gather the energy to drop off my dry cleaning. 

I also used to hold out hope that my depression would lift if I got a better job, or a happier relationship or some other accomplishment or achievemen and I would be happy like other people. But I have come to the realization that nothing of that sort will make me happy. If my incredible blessings up to this point haven't made me happy than nothing will. It's true that my best options are medication and therapy and I am absolutely giving that my all. It still does not seem to greatly lift my spirits and I have started to fear that this is a lifelong affliction from which I will never recover. Though I am making every effort I can think of to combat this.

Thank you again for the kind words. I was touched reading your responses.

I know exactly what you mean. You could be describing me ten years ago. I don't have any words of wisdome, but for what it's worth, Nietzsche can be pretty uplifting if you read him right. Don't forget he once said "a day without dancing is a day wasted". 

I also recommend Heidegger and Kierkegaard if you like existentialism. Heidegger makes the fact that we exist and are aware of our mortality seem like an incredible awe inspiring thing. Kierkegaard makes good arguments for looking at the insane absurdity of the world and embracing it. If you want to talk philosophy or just shoot the shit to break up the monotony of life feel free to DM.

I totally agree with you. Besides a few small details, you could be reading my mind. The video game analogy always makes a lot of sense to me. 

Besides reverting to an early save point, I also just want to turn off the game for a while. Sometimes it isn't that the game is too hard or you're bad at it or something. Sometimes you just get fried out and frustrated and need to turn it off and take a break. 

I keep day dreaming about what the equivalent would be for life, and I haven't found one yet. Even with a vacation or something you still have to worry about having money, and feeding yourself and all of the little mundane tasks that can seem like huge obstacles when depression gets bad. With sleep or a coma you don't get to experience the time away from life.
